items.tweet_text:
From the Bilateral Meeting in Beijing:

President Trump had a good meeting with President Xi of China. https://t.co/WaH8hR1ZV3

description.text: A text-only statement card with a dark navy textured (linen/canvas-grain) background. The body text is centered and set in a small light-grey/cream serif typeface, formatted as a centered paragraph block. At the bottom, in spaced small-caps cream lettering, is the wordmark 'THE WHITE HOUSE'. There is no photograph or illustration. The full on-image text reads: 'President Trump had a good meeting with President Xi of China. The two sides discussed ways to enhance economic cooperation between our two countries, including expanding market access for American businesses into China and increasing Chinese investment into our industries. Leaders from many of the United States' largest companies joined a portion of the meeting. The Presidents also highlighted the need to build on progress in ending the flow of fentanyl precursors into the United States, as well as increasing Chinese purchases of American agricultural products. The two sides agreed that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open to support the free flow of energy. President Xi also made clear China's opposition to the militarization of the Strait and any effort to charge a toll for its use, and he expressed interest in purchasing more American oil to reduce China's dependence on the Strait in the future. Both countries agreed that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon. THE WHITE HOUSE'.

MEDIA LIES: "ICE detained a 5-year-old"

FACTS: A criminal illegal alien ABANDONED his child as he fled from ICE officers, and our officers ensured the child was kept SAFE in the bitter cold. Vice President @JDVance explains why context matters:

description.text: Four video keyframes show JD Vance speaking at a podium with uniformed personnel and flags behind him. A television-style caption bar appears along the bottom.

transcript.text: Well, I'm proud of the fact that we're standing behind law enforcement, and I'm proud of the fact that we're enforcing the country's laws. But, you know, you asked a question about this five-year-old kid. I actually saw this terrible story while I was coming to Minneapolis. We just left Toledo a high this morning for an economic messaging event. And I see this story, and I'm a father of a five-year-old. Actually, a five-year-old little boy, and I think to myself, oh my God, this is terrible. How did we arrest the five-year-old? Well, I do a little bit more follow-up research. And what I find is that the five-year-old was not arrested. That his dad was an illegal alien. And then when they went to arrest his illegal alien father, the father ran. So, the story is that ICE detained a five-year-old. Well, what are they supposed to do? Are they supposed to let a five-year-old child freeze to death? Are they not supposed to arrest an illegal alien in the United States of America? If the argument is that you can't arrest people who have violated our laws because they have children, then every single parent is going to be completely given immunity from ever being the subject of law enforcement. That doesn't make any sense. No one thinks that makes any sense. Now, you know, there are so many of these cases like that where if you just understand the context, there have been a number of situations that I've looked into, personally, where I say, wait a second, we don't want ICE and arresting American citizens. They're supposed to be enforcing the immigration laws against the legal aliens. So then I look into it, and I find out that the American citizen who was arrested took a swing at an ICE officer. You can't have that happen. And, of course, they have to defend themselves. And, of course, they have the right to detain somebody who assaults a law enforcement officer. Now, this is my point. Do we want these things to happen? Do we want these arrests to be so chaotic? No, we don't. These guys want at least to fall. But if we had a little cooperation from local and state officials, I think the chaos would go way down in this community.

items.tweet_text: .@POTUS on the newly announced White House ballroom: "We've been planning it for a long time. They've wanted a ballroom at the White House for more than 150 years... I'm good at building things and we'll get it built quickly and on time." https://t.co/fhbv3LXGFT

description.text: A news-style video frame shows President Trump speaking at a lectern indoors, with suited officials standing behind him in a formal room.

transcript.text: Yeah, Mr. President, can you talk about your plans for the new ballroom that was announced today? Yeah. And the $200 million, that's going to be paid for by yourself as well. By me? Yeah. It's a private thing. I'll do it, and we'll probably have some donors or whatever, but it's about 200 million. So we've been planning it for a long time. They've wanted a ballroom at the White House for more than 150 years. But there's never been a president that was good at ballrooms. I'm really good. In fact, I looked at one that we just built in Turnberry and Scotland, and it's incredible. We're good at building. I'm good at building things, and we'll get it built quickly. And on time, it'll be beautiful, top of the line. We've retained the best architects and engineers, everything else. It'll be built over on the east side, and it will be beautiful. It'll be views of the Washington Monument. It wanted to fear with the current building. It won't be near it, but not touching it. And pays total respect to the existing building, which I'm the biggest fan of. It's my favorite place. I love it. But they've wanted it. And, you know, when they have big events, you entertain the president of China, or the president of any place. And you have big crowds. They've always had to get a tent. And you've probably been to some of them, Bobby, when it rains, it's a disaster. And the tents are 100 yards. It's more than a football field away from the main entrance. And people are slopping down to the tent. It's not a pretty sight. The women with their lovely evening gowns, all of their hair, all done. And they're a mess by the time they get. And they've always wanted to have it. And I said, you know, in the first term, I said, you know, if I get another shot at this, I'm going to do a ballroom. I was pretty busy in the first, because I was running the country. And I was also fighting for survival with all of the lunatics I had to beat. But it worked out, obviously, it worked out very well because here we are. But I always said I was going to do something about the ballroom because they should have one. So we'll be leaving it. It'll be a great legacy project. And I think it'll be special. You saw some renderings of the initial. I think it'll be really beautiful. No government tell us now.

"To fight the bug, we must understand the bug."

CBP agriculture specialists in Detroit found fresh cherries infested with European cherry fruit fly maggots and larvae. The traveler who had the infested cherries was headed to Door County, Wisconsin, a major cherry growing area. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Ohio CINCINNATI-A Cincinnati man who was arrested in July after he allegedly made multiple threats online to shoot and kill ICE officers has now been indicted by a federal grand jury. Anthony Marcus Kelly, 38, is charged in a two-count indictment with making threats to assault or murder a United States official and with making threatening interstate communications. According to charging documents, from June 26 through July 17, Kelly allegedly used the social media username “Slab” and made multiple social media posts calling for the killing of ICE officers and detailing his acquisition of firearms to carry out that threat. Inone of his alleged posts, Kelly wrote “Why even bother with these damn courts anymore. #Gestapedos don't deserve anything but the smoke coming for them anyway. #RevolutionlsTheSolution #DestroyICE they're rabid dogs that need to be put down. Including #KristiNoem #DogmeatWalking” In another, he wrote, “You come here for me, you're getting shot. And Im not looking to disable [...] 'm shooting for the kill. won't give a **** about your names, who you are, or anything else”. Kelly was arrested on July 22 and remains in federal custody. Threatening to assault or murder a United States official is a federal crime punishable by up to 10 years in prison. Making threatening interstate communications carries a potential penalty of up to five years in prison. Dominick S. Gerace Il, United States Attorney for the Southern District of Ohio, HSI Detroit acting Special Agent in Charge Jared Murphey and FBI Cincinnati Special Agent in Charge Elena latarola. Criminal Chief Christy L. Muncy is representing the United States in this case. An indictment merely contains allegations, and defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law.

Members of the Denver Special Response Team stopped to help with a 4-vehicle accident on their way to our Broadview Detention Center in Chicago, Sept. 26. 

Smoke poured out of one of the vehicles and an unconscious man, covered in blood, was trapped inside.  

Our officers rescued the man using breaching equipment because his legs were pinned. They were able to extract him just before the vehicle was engulfed in flame. They rendered aid until EMS arrived at the scene. 

ICE commends the brave actions of these officers. 

➡️See more photos in our newsroom.

We're advancing American energy dominance through nuclear leadership. NNSA produced 325 kilograms of high assay, lowered rich uranium, or HALU, and provided it to the Office of Nuclear Energy for powering advanced reactor projects. Recently, NNSA secured a record 1.7 metric tons of HALU from Japan, the largest single international uranium shipment in NNSA history. In Ohio, we are transforming the historic Port Smith gaseous diffusion site into a powerful hub that will create thousands of jobs and drive long-term innovation and investment in the community. description.text: Four keyframes show a military history montage with official seals, black-and-white archival photographs, portraits, and text overlays. The smaller captions are not readable on the sheet.

transcript.text: Welcome to this week's reflective moments of America's military, a weekly segment where we take you through the US military's 250-year history. On January 30, 1968, over 80,000 North Vietnamese and Viet Cong troops launched a surprise on more than 100 cities and towns across South Vietnam, ranging from provincial capitals to the US Embassy in Saigon. However, US forces and South Vietnamese troops responded to the attacks, beat back the offensive, and eventually recaptured the territory. On February 3, 1943, the US Army transport doorchester, a former coastal passenger steamship requisitioned by the Army crossed the Northern Atlantic and was struck by a German torpedo. As the ship sank, four Army chaplains, ministers George L. Fox and Clark V. Poling, priest John P. Washington and Rabbi Alexander B. Goat, began tending to soldiers and guiding them to safety. As lifefests ran out, the chaplains each chose to give theirs to another soldier, in an act that would earn them all a posthumous, distinguished service cross and purple heart. On February 5, 1917, following a year-long expedition deep into the heart of Mexico, in search of Mexican revolutionary leader Pachovia, Army general John Blackjack Pershing, and his troops crossed back into the United States after being recalled. The expedition provided experience in mobilization and logistics, particularly in the use of motorized vehicles and aircraft. These skills would prove invaluable soon on the battlefields of Europe as the US was on the verge of entering World War I. This has been this week's reflective moments of America's military. Visit our website for more information and be sure to check back next week for more.

ocr.text: OFFICE OF CHAIRMAN BRENDAN CARR FCC Secures Win for America’s Leadership in Next-Gen Connectivity Accelerates Internet Speeds, Bolsters Competition, Enhances Direct-to-Device WASHINGTON, May 12, 2026—Today, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr announced that the agency approved two transactions that will further secure U.S. leadership in wireless and next-gen technology, including emerging direct-to-device (D2D) offerings. The two transactions— collectively surpassing $40 billion in deal value—will allow the private sector to light up a large swath of approximately 115 megahertz of underused mid-band spectrum for the benefit of the American people. Specifically, the FCC’s Wireless Telecommunications Bureau and Space Bureau approved EchoStar’s sale of approximately 65 megahertz of spectrum to SpaceX and an additional 50 megahertz to AT&T. These two decisions promise to accelerate Internet speeds, strengthen competition, and bolster rural service while allowing America to lead the world in next-gen connectivity, including new high-speed offerings direct to your smartphone from low-earth orbit satellites. «Lights Up Prime, Mid-Band Spectrum for Faster Broadband: Valuable mid-band spectrum will move to providers motivated to expand offerings for the American people. AT&T will accelerate its 5G and fixed wireless deployment to support in-home broadband as well as manufacturing hubs, energy sectors, and small businesses. Indeed, immediately after annoucing the sale, AT&T received special authority to light up EchoStar’s 3.45 GHz spectram—and within weeks, the spectrum was deployed across 23,000 sites and boosted 5G download speeds by up to 80 percent nationwide. Looking to the future, the FCC’s decisions impose buildout obligations to ensure the spectrum benefits consumers, accelerates next-gen connectivity, and fosters increased competition within wireless and satellite markets. « Advances America’s Global Leadership in Next-Gen D2D Offerings: The FCC is advancing a series of reforms to match the innovation and investment in direct-to-device (D2D) services. D2D allows smartphones and IoT devices to connect directly to satellites for seamless, high- speed coverage everywhere, especially in remote and underserved areas. Several weeks ago, two significant decisions from the Space Bureau: (1) approved AST SpaceMobile’s competitive 248- satellite D2D system; and (2) confirmed the exclusive nature of D2D spectrum bands, including the spectrum SpaceX is acquiring from EchoStar. Now with today’s decision, SpaceX gains access—for the first time ever—to exclusive-use, contiguous spectrum nationwide for a Starlink D2D service and other offerings. * Bolsters Competition, Promoting Affordable Service. Together, both transactions promise to reshape the wireless industry with new, disruptive competition that drives down prices for American consumers. By supercharging America’s leadership in D2D services, more consumers will have more choices in more places. transcript.text: Welcome to this week's reflective moments of America's military, a weekly segment where we take you through some of the major events from the US military's 250-year history. February 13th marks the birth of General Chuck Yeager, a key figure in US military aviation history. A World War II flying ace, Yeager later became the first person to break the sound barrier in 1947, proving supersonic flight was possible and transforming military air power. On February 16th, we recognize President's Day. Military service has been a common path for many American presidents. Since the first president, George Washington's leadership has set the precedent for the soldier statesmen, along many others, including Andrew Jackson, Ulysses S. Grant, Theodore Roosevelt, Dwight D. Eisenhower, John F. Kennedy, and George H. W. Bush, who have carried these traditions from their time in uniform to the president's office. On February 19th, 1945, the volcanic island of Ivojima became the stage for one of World War II's most historic battles, when US Marines of the 4th and 5th divisions landed on the black sand beaches. On February 23rd, when a group of Marines raised an American flag atop Mount Surabachi, it became one of the most famous historic photographs. Weeks after the flag raising, the battle officially ended on March 26th with an American victory. And this has been this week's reflective moments of America's military. Visit our website to learn more and stay tuned for more next week.

transcript.text: Hi everyone, Secretary Laurie Chavez-Duremer here. As we close out 2025, I want to take a moment to wish you a happy new year. It has been an honor to serve all of you. America's workers and retirees, during my first year, as your Secretary of Labor. I'm grateful for your dedication and hard work. At the Department of Labor, we wasted no time fulfilling President Trump's goal of putting the American worker first. We fought to keep workers safe on the job, secure their hard earned benefits, expand access to training and employment opportunities, and so much more. For example, we registered almost 300,000 new apprentices, launched compliance assistant programs to help employers succeed and unveiled project firewall to ensure companies don't displace US workers with cheaper foreign labor. As we look ahead to 2026, the Department of Labor will build on this momentum and continue to put American workers first. On behalf of everyone here at the Department of Labor, I'm happy new year.

transcript.text: Second rescue mission involved 155 aircraft including four bombers, 64 fighters, 48 refueling tankers, 13 rescue aircraft and more. We were bringing them all over and a lot of it was subterfuge. We wanted to have them think he was in a different location because they had a vast military force out there. Thousands of people were looking. So we wanted them to look in different areas so we were scattered all over like we were right on top of them. We had seven different locations where they thought and they were very confused. They said, well, wait a minute. They've got groups here. They've got groups there. It's an amazing thing. I was listening to these great people, these great generals, General Raisin Cairn was amazing and Pete Hexeth was amazing. But I listened to the whole thing. It was pretty amazing so that all these different sites where everybody thought he was located. We think we have them over there because they have nine planes circling a little area. That's 25 miles down the coast.

.@ICEgov arrests alleged MS-13 associate wanted for aggravated homicide in El Salvador— @DHSgov says Idalia Isabel Morales-Mejia is an illegal immigrant wanted in El Salvador for aggravated homicide and identified as an associate of MS-13 —She was arrested in Northern Virginia.

Authorities say Morales-Mejia was charged in El Salvador back in 2013 and later entered the U.S. illegally at an unknown time and location.

She was located and arrested in Woodbridge after updated intel from El Salvador’s fugitive task force.

ICE Washington, D.C. will continue to prioritize public safety by arresting and removing criminal alien offenders from our Washington, D.C. and Virginia communities.”

ICE says she is now in custody pending immigration proceedings.

items.tweet_text: Stacey embraces her heritage by making dishes from her family’s hometown in the Basque region of Spain for holiday family dinners. She’s proud of where she comes from and happy her parents were accepted in America with open arms. #ImmigrantHeritageMonth https://t.co/fOJu4xrWCa

description.text: Graphic with a deep navy-blue background, a faint large American-flag watermark, and the white bold headline 'DHS Celebrates National Immigrant Heritage Month' at top. Centered is a rectangular color photo of three women posing together; the middle woman wears a black cap and gown and holds a diploma, flanked by two other women in casual and business-casual dress, standing outdoors near a storefront. Below a large white quotation mark, the white text reads: "My immigrant story starts with my father immigrating to the United States in 1947. The white circular DHS (U.S. Department of Homeland Security) seal sits to the right of the text. A thin horizontal red rule separates the headline from a bold all-caps white word 'FACT SHEET' at the bottom with a drop shadow. No photographs; purely typographic.

items.tweet_text: Yahor immigrated with his family from Belarus while also completing university studies in Lithuania. Upon his graduation, he served in the @USArmy for four years followed by joining @CBP. He dedicates his life to showing his gratitude to live in “the greatest country on earth.” https://t.co/4V8j4yk3Jt

description.text: DHS 'National Immigrant Heritage Month' spotlight card with a deep navy-blue background and a faint large American flag as a watermark. The white headline at top reads 'DHS Celebrates National Immigrant Heritage Month.' Centered is a rectangular portrait of a man in a dark CBP (Customs and Border Protection) uniform with a badge, standing in front of an American flag and a second flag, name tape partly visible. Below a large white quotation mark is text in white serif: "My entire life in the U.S. is dedicated to showing my gratitude for the opportunity to live in the greatest country on Earth. Every day, I am thankful for the chance and the green card we received in 2013. I have achieved a lot and aim to achieve even more, contributing to making the U.S. stronger and more resilient." A blue rounded banner at bottom-left reads: 'Yahor S. / CBP, Customs and Border Protection Officer / 1st generation from Republic of Belarus.' The circular DHS seal is at bottom-right.

items.tweet_text: In FY24, @CBP officers and agents processed over 400 million travelers while seizing nearly 22,000 pounds of fentanyl, keeping our borders secure and communities safe. This holiday season, they continue their critical work, protecting our nation and ensuring lawful trade and travel. Thank you for your dedication to protecting our nation and ensuring lawful trade and travel every day. #5DaysofThanks
